subject: Staging->Prod VPC migration readiness checklist
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Park <erin.park@novadata.com>, ops@novadata.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Staging->Prod VPC migration readiness checklist

Team / Erin,

Following our run-through last week, attached is the canonical staging->prod migration checklist we'll use for the Private VPC cutover this Friday. High-level plan below and asks in bold. Please confirm by EOD that the items you own are green.

Summary (target cutover window):
- Date: 2026-09-24
- Canary window: 30 minutes (10% traffic), rollback triggers defined
- Full cutover: 2 hour maintenance window, with ops on-call

Immediate asks for Nova Data Systems (Erin / ops@novadata.com):
1) Confirm a 60-minute maintenance notice window from your end for client-facing services.
2) Provide the list of firewall rules that require exceptions to allow egress from our onprem nodes (we need exact ports + CIDRs) — please reply with a CSV if possible.
3) Any additional upstream NAT IPs that require allowlisting beyond the list in the Drive link below.

Key cutover items (owners):
- Pre-checks: routing, BGP sessions, control-plane reachability (Logan)
- Egress NAT mapping & firewall exceptions (Erin / Nova ops)
- KV-cache warmup and model snapshot pinning (Kimberly)
- Traffic shift + health-check policy (Marcus)

Attachments: staging-to-prod-checklist.xlsx (master checklist). Diagrams and reference runbook live here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_diagrams

I'll queue an ops bridge at T-30m before the canary window. If anything in the checklist doesn't map cleanly to your internal change control, call it out and we'll adjust timing.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Staging->Prod VPC migration readiness checklist

Marcus,

Thanks — schedule looks reasonable. A couple of clarifying questions from our networking team: 

- Cutover window: can we shift the full cutover start to 02:00–04:00 local to avoid peak analytics loads? Our preference is 03:00 local. Is that compatible with your on-call rotation?
- Firewall exceptions: we can provide the CSV. Do you need source CIDRs (clients) or destination CIDRs (your egress NATs)? We usually permit destination ranges in our perimeter policy.
- BGP: we need your ASNs and expected local-pref changes for the 10% canary. Also confirm whether you plan to announce backup prefixes during the canary.

We also saw in the diagrams there are two egress paths (public NAT and transit-proxy). During canary, should both be enabled or should traffic prefer the transit-proxy only?

I'll pull the firewall team into a follow-up if helpful; ops@novadata.com is on copy.

Best,
Erin Park
Platform Ops Manager, Nova Data Systems
erin.park@novadata.com
+1 (206) 555-0199
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Park <erin.park@novadata.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:20:05 +0000
Subject: Re: Staging->Prod VPC migration readiness checklist

Erin — thanks for the quick questions. Answers below and attached artifacts.

1) Cutover local time: 03:00 local for you is OK for our ops rotation; Marcus and I will be on the bridge. I'll update the checklist times to reflect 03:00–05:00 local (03:30 canary).

2) Firewall exceptions: please provide destination CIDRs — that's what we need to be reachable from your perimeter. Attached is egress-ip-list.csv with the three NAT IPs we expect to use. If you need additional /32s for transient autoscaling nodes we can add them but prefer to keep the list minimal.

3) BGP and announcements: Our ASNs are AS65041 (primary) and AS65042 (backup). For canary we will not announce backup prefixes — we will keep announcements as-is and rely on path-preference and route-maps to direct ~10% traffic to the new VPC nodes. I'll paste the planned route-map snippet into the runbook.

4) Dual egress paths: For the canary we recommend using transit-proxy only (control throttles and observability hooks are in the proxy). Public NAT path will remain configured but marked as lower-preference; full traffic shift will enable NAT path.

Attachments: egress-ip-list.csv (3 rows), runbook-cutover.md (cutover runbook, 8 pages). Drive diagrams also updated: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_diagrams

Onboarding items we still need from Nova: the maintenance notice confirmation, and a named POC on firewall approvals.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Deployment Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

All — great progress. Final confirmations and next steps below.

Confirmed schedule: 2026-09-24, 03:00–05:00 local (03:30 canary start, 03:30–04:00 canary window). Ops bridge will be on Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/999-888-777 (passcode sent to POC).

Nova deliverables (Erin / ops):
- Destination CIDRs (firewall CSV) by 09/22 18:00 local — THANKS for agreeing to provide.
- Named approver for the firewall change (we need the approver's name/email for our change ticket).

Redwood deliverables (internal):
- Logan: verify BGP route-map snippet in runbook and coordinate with your NOC at T-60m.
- Kimberly: snapshot model versions and pre-warm KV cache (T-90m).
- Laura: run the pre-cutover checklist and confirm all green 30m before canary.

Rollback triggers (abbreviated):
- If 4xx/5xx rate >3x baseline for 5 minutes during canary -> rollback to staging and withdraw announcements.
- Latency p95 degradation >150ms for 10 minutes -> pause shift and reconvene.

I'll open a Jira change INFRA-4821 for the cutover notes and attach the runbook. Please post the firewall CSV to this ticket or reply to this thread so Laura can pick it up.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth cutover.

Marcus
